questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests knowledge of per-namespace configuration, ConfigMaps, and rolling updates without image rebuilds.

## Key Concepts

- ConfigMaps for environment-specific config
- Pod env refs via ConfigMapKeyRef
- Mounting ConfigMaps as files via volumes
- CI-friendly updates and rolling restarts

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: web-config
  namespace: web
data:
  ENV: "staging"
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
  namespace: web
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web-app
        image: web-app:latest
        env:
        - name: ENV
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: web-config
              key: ENV
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /etc/web/config
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: web-config
          items:
          - key: ENV
            path: env
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle config changes that require pod restart vs. hot reload?
- What if you need multiple environments with isolated values?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mastery of Kubernetes primitives and safe release strategies using only built‑in resources.

## Key Concepts
- Blue-green deployments
- Deployments, Services, and selectors
- Readiness checks and quick rollback
- Observability of the switchover

## Code Example
```yaml
# blue Deployment (conceptual)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app-blue
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: myapp, color: blue}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: myapp, color: blue}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v1
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 80}
```

```yaml
# green Deployment (conceptual)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app-green
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: myapp, color: green}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: myapp, color: green}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v2
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 80}
```

```yaml
# Service routing to whichever color is live
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  selector:
    app: myapp
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate a rollback without impacting users?
- What metrics/logs would you monitor during the switch and post-switch stability?

## Why This Is Asked
Beginner multi-tenant scenario focusing on namespace boundaries, enforcing limits, and validating in CI.

## Key Concepts
- ResourceQuota
- LimitRange
- Namespace isolation
- CI verification of quota enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# ResourceQuota for team-a
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: team-a-quota
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    pods: "10"
    requests.cpu: "20"
    requests.memory: "40Gi"
    limits.cpu: "40"
    limits.memory: "80Gi"
```
```yaml
# LimitRange for team-a
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: team-a-limits
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: "500m"
      memory: "512Mi"
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: "500m"
      memory: "512Mi"
    min:
      cpu: "100m"
      memory: "128Mi"
    max:
      cpu: "2"
      memory: "2Gi"
    type: Container
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adjust if a specific workload requires higher limits?  
- How would you monitor quota usage over time and alert on nearing limits?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical exposure to Kubernetes networking end-to-end: services, ingress routing, DNS, and basic validation. It avoids high-level definitions and assesses concrete implementation decisions.

## Key Concepts
- Service types and port mappings
- Ingress routing rules and path types

## Code Example
```yaml
# widget-svc.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: widget-svc
spec:
  selector:
    app: widget
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
```
```yaml
# widget-ingress.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: widget-ingress
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: nginx
spec:
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - widget.example.com
    secretName: widget-tls
  rules:
  - host: widget.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /v1/*
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: widget-svc
            port:
```
